chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa', from Ali ibn Maysara, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

Verily, the seed of the believer may reside in the loins of the polytheist man, and no evil shall befall it; until when it transfers to the womb of the polytheist woman, no evil befalls her; until she gives birth to him. And when she gives birth to him, no evil befalls him until the Pen flows upon him.

key_terms.الشر: Al-Sharr — evil or harm, including spiritual and physical affliction
key_terms.القلم: Al-Qalam — 'the Pen', a metaphor for divine recording of deeds and the onset of legal/moral accountability (taklif)
key_terms.المؤمن: Al-Mu'min — the believer, one who has true faith (iman)
key_terms.المشرك: Al-Mushrik — the polytheist or one who associates partners with God
key_terms.رحم: Rahim — the womb, the maternal vessel of gestation
key_terms.صلب: Sulb — the loins or spinal column, symbolizing paternal lineage
key_terms.نطفة: Nutfa — the seminal drop/seed, the initial stage of human creation

ai.seo_question: Can a child of a believer be born from polytheist parents according to al-Kafi?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) teaches that the spiritual essence of a believer is divinely protected throughout the process of gestation, even when carried in the bodies of non-believers. This hadith affirms that true faith is not inherited through physical lineage but is an innate, God-given disposition (fitra) that God safeguards from the moment of its potential existence. The 'flowing of the Pen' is a classical Islamic metaphor for the commencement of personal moral accountability, typically understood to begin at puberty.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan in Ali Al Washa, from Ali Bin Maysara who said, 
‘Abu Abdullah<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said:

‘The seed of the Believer may exit in the back of the Polytheist man, so it would not be hit by anything from the evil until it comes to be in a womb of the Polytheist woman, and it would not be hit by anything from the evil until she give his birth. So when she does give him birth, nothing from the evil would hit him until the Pen flows against him’ (until he reaches adulthood and becomes responsible for his acts).
en.sarwar: 1. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu’ alia ibn Muhammad from al- Hassan ibn Ali al-Washsha’ from Ali ibn Maysara who has said the following:“Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said,

‘The seed for a believer may exist in the back of a pagan and no evil affects it until it is transferred into the womb of a pagan woman wherein no evil affects it also. It is not affected even after birth and up to the time the person is considered responsible for his/her deeds.’”
